name: Haas UMC-500
description: 40-taper 5-axis universal machining centre: bridge-type X/Y/Z spindle head with a B (tilt) / C (rotary) trunnion table.
sources: Haas UMC series operator's manual supplement - axis definitions, settings 254-257, safe zones
Haas UMC geometry guide - B axis of rotation is parallel to the Y-Z plane
Haas UMC-500 published specification: X 610 mm, Y 406 mm, Z 406 mm, B +120/-35 deg, C 360 deg, 400 mm platter

mrzp.source: Placeholder at the travel centre. Replace with the machine's Settings 255 (X), 256 (Y), 257 (Z) and 254 (5-axis rotary centre distance).

rotaryConvention.note: Table axes follow the ISO primed-axis convention: a positive B or C command turns the table so that the tool moves positively about +Y / +Z relative to the part. Flip `sense` on the b-trunnion or c-platter node if a test move on the machine shows the opposite direction.
rotaryConvention.evidence: The machine's orbit-home macro O09013 (HaasUMCmemory/09000) moves a table point p to MRZP + Ry(-B) Rz(-C) (p - MRZP) when it builds G59 for a tilted plane, which is sense -1 on both trunnion nodes.

workOffsets.note: Work offsets that the program or the initial macro variables do not define (#5221-#5326, #7001+, #14001+) are placed at the MRZP with B0 C0.

parameterVariables.note: Machine parameters read by macros (#30000-#39999), keyed by macro variable. 30057.25 (parameter 57 bit 25, negative work offsets) must be 1 for the Renishaw macros in the machine memory, which alarm otherwise. Parameters not listed read 0.

kinematics.description: X saddle on the bridge, Y ram, Z spindle head; B trunnion tilts about a line parallel to Y through the MRZP and carries the C platter.
